generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: OVER 2,500 ORGANIZATIONS IMPACTED BY LITELLM SUPPLY CHAIN ATTACK
Summary: TeamPCP compromised LiteLLM after its CI pipeline automatically installed a trojanized Trivy release. LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 ran malicious code on every Python invocation. The packages were live for 40 minutes, exposing 434,000 CI/CD pipelines across 2,500 organizations. Treat LiteLLM-accessible credentials as exposed. Validate and rotate secrets, accounts, and sessions, then review logs.

Editorial idea:
A trusted software supply chain becomes the route through which a brief compromise reaches thousands of organizations.

Central subject:
The LiteLLM package supply-chain attack

Visual relationship:
A trojanized dependency at the center connects outward to 2,500 organizations and 434,000 exposed CI/CD pipelines, showing how one compromised link can propagate through software production.

Composition:
Show a single compromised package moving along a branching chain of software build steps toward many separated workplaces, with the short 40-minute exposure window contrasted against the wide spread of affected systems.

Permitted literal elements:
A software package archive
A CI/CD pipeline represented by connected build stages
Branching paths toward many organization markers
A visible but non-textual indication of a short exposure window
Separated credentials or access tokens positioned along the affected paths

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Decorative server racks
Generic computer screens
Logos
Rendered text
Unsupported physical details
Arrows used as the sole explanation of flow

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting the attack as a single isolated computer infection
Suggesting all 434,000 pipelines were breached rather than exposed
Making the 40-minute package availability period visually insignificant
Using generic cyberattack imagery without showing the supply-chain relationship

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
